lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Raised forecast accuracy from 70% to 85% by switching the MAPE calculation to cover only SKUs that sold every week.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; my findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.
- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations, raising inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5% within a year.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Cut inbound freight cost per pallet from $48 to $41 over two quarters by consolidating supplier pickups into four regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.

- Scoring 40 vendors weekly on on-time delivery, fill rate, lead-time variance and invoice accuracy, and sharing the scorecards with buyers before each quarterly review, raised on-time inbound deliveries from 81% to 93%.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Trained 6 planners on the new forecasting workflow and wrote its exception-handling guide, which the team still uses for promotions.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Cut average route length from 120 to 90 miles, a 40% reduction, by solving the routing problem with customer time windows.
- Raised on-time deliveries by 9% in simulation, from 84% to 93%, by adding customer time windows to the routing model.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Wrote a slotting guide that the volunteer coordinators used to re-slot the warehouse again after its spring expansion.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Experience should appear above Education.
items.because: Several years of relevant work give a recruiter more current evidence of your qualifications than the degree.

items.says: Experience is not in reverse chronological order.
items.because: Lakeview appears above the more recent Crestway role, making the work history harder to scan.

items.says: The current florist role takes space without explaining how it fits the career direction.
The delivery bullet gives volume but no outcome showing the effect of the deliveries.
The verbs use past tense for a role listed as current.
The wedding and cooler duties have no stated outcome.
The verbs use past tense for a role listed as current.
The stated accuracy increase is not supported by changing the SKU population used in the MAPE calculation.
items.because: The increase could reflect the narrower SKU set rather than improved forecasting.

items.says: The processing-time result is buried after the study setup.
items.because: A reader may notice the time study before the reduction from 3 days to 1.

items.says: The phrase uses a personal pronoun.
Your role in establishing the triage station is unclear.
The scheduling-rules detail does not show what operational change the rules introduced.
The bullet repeats “dock” in “at the dock.”
The dock-scheduling bullet should appear before the other Lakeview bullets.
The inventory-accuracy figures do not identify the population measured.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the comparison covers the 2,000 high-value locations or the wider inventory.

items.says: The seasonal-model description does not identify its distinguishing technique or input.
The reorder-point bullet describes work and review cadence but gives no result.
The opening gerund does not fit grammatically with the past-tense main verb.
items.because: “Scoring” does not connect grammatically to “raised,” making the sentence harder to follow.

items.says: The inbound-delivery result comes after a long method description.
items.because: Readers must work through the scoring and scorecard details before finding the 81% to 93% improvement.

items.says: The reported OEE of 112% is invalid under the standard definition.
items.because: Availability, performance and quality are each capped at 100%, so their product cannot exceed 100%.

items.says: The bullet names the losses reduced but not the intervention used to reduce them.
The sentence does not say what the workflow or guide improved.
“Its” could refer to either the forecasting workflow or the exception-handling guide.
The two route-distance figures are presented as the same improvement, but their reductions differ.
items.because: One bullet reports 18% and the next reports 40%, leaving it unclear whether the measures differ or the figures are inconsistent.

items.says: The route-distance result is repeated across two bullets.
items.because: Presenting both as separate routing-model results can seem repetitive and obscure whether they are distinct measures.

items.says: The route-length change is a 25% reduction, not a 40% reduction.
items.because: The 30-mile decrease is 25% of the original 120 miles.

items.says: The route-length bullet should appear before the other project bullets if retained.
items.because: The review identifies it as the strongest line, and moving it earlier would give its quantified result more prominence.

items.says: The customer-time-window method is repeated across the route-length and on-time-delivery bullets.
The on-time-delivery change is 9 percentage points, not an unqualified 9%.
The summary does not say whether the recommendations were adopted or what changed.
The analysis description does not identify what you examined or how.
The donation-intake result uses passive voice and does not identify who mapped the process.
“A day sooner” does not identify the comparison behind the time improvement.
The donation-intake result should be moved ahead of the general analysis bullet.
The slotting-guide bullet shows adoption but not what the re-slotting achieved.
The bullet does not say what informed the slotting recommendations.
“Again” repeats the idea that the warehouse was re-slotted.
